431289.mechanism: OVER-EXCLUSION, not a collision fix. Target watches services.prosody.muc.moderation (option_prefix=[services,prosody,muc]). Real source confirmed (prosody.nix @ head cea3dfac9e5a4bcc13100623be892a37b2d80c2b): `mucOpts = _: { options = { ...; moderation = mkOption {...}; }; };` (a named, let-bound function value, lines 299-376), used via `muc = mkOption { type = types.listOf (types.submodule mucOpts); ... };` (line 819-820) -- a REAL option declared exactly at option_prefix's own concrete relativized path (services.prosody.muc), directly type-referencing mucOpts. This is the LEGITIMATE way this concrete option_prefix's own contents are declared (via listOf(submodule <name>), analogous to kimai's attrsOf(submodule siteOpts) but for a list rather than an attrset), not an unrelated auxiliary construct. F1's fix cannot currently distinguish 'named submodule genuinely unrelated to option_prefix' (angrr's real defect) from 'named submodule that IS option_prefix's own real declared content, referenced by name rather than inline' (this case) -- both are 'a top-level options={} block nested inside a named let/rec binding, not inside a tracked mkOption call', which is the ONLY thing is_nested_inside_named_let_or_rec_binding actually checks. Effect: head regresses from the historically-correct PredicateNotFound (declaration genuinely found, no test ever witnesses it) to the WRONG OptionNotFound (declaration falsely reported as not existing at all), collapsing a real historical VerdictChanged into a false Unchanged -- the opposite failure mode from angrr, but the same code path.
